resources.string: Mirrors your phone. Android asks for screen-capture consent, and anything visible on your phone may appear on the receiver.
Uses scrcpy to create a separate display for apps while you use your phone. Support varies by device and app. Protected content may not work; optional audio may include sound from the whole device.

Mirra casts your Android device to a compatible Miracast receiver over Wi-Fi Direct. Turn on Wi-Fi and make sure the receiver is ready to accept a wireless display connection.\n\nYou can reopen this guide from the menu.

Install and start Shizuku before casting. Shizuku provides Mirra with the shell access needed to prepare casting and run the external-display server. Follow the instructions in the Shizuku app to start it using wireless debugging, ADB, or root, as supported by your device.\n\nAllow Mirra when Shizuku asks for permission. Depending on how you start Shizuku, you may need to start it again after restarting your phone.

Current screen mirrors what is on your phone. Android will ask for screen-capture consent; anything visible on the phone may appear on the receiver.\n\nExternal screen uses scrcpy to create a separate virtual display. Apps can open there while you use your phone. External display and desktop windowing support vary by device and app; some apps or protected content may not work. Optional external audio can include sound from the whole device.

While an external screen is casting, open Controller to use the touchpad, launch apps, and open the TV remote or gamepad. Use two fingers to scroll or pinch to zoom.\n\nThe TV remote and gamepad use virtual HID devices on Android 15 or newer; support and game compatibility vary. The gamepad has two sticks and supports moving and resizing controls in Edit mode. Triggers are full-press controls, not pressure sensitive.

If a receiver will not connect, try the other connection style: Shared lets the devices negotiate the host; Forced host asks the phone to host. Shared is often better for TVs, and Forced host can help with Windows, but results vary. Long-press a device to clear its remembered choice.\n\nSaved Wi-Fi Direct groups can also cause failures, especially with Windows receivers. Open Wi-Fi Direct settings from Mirra’s menu and manually remove saved groups if needed, then retry. Mirra does not delete them automatically. Some devices, receivers, and content may not support casting.

Mirra is made by BlueCartoonCat and licensed under Apache 2.0. Explore the Mirra repository.

Shizuku by RikkaApps provides shell access. See its repository and Apache 2.0 license.

scrcpy by Genymobile powers the external screen. See its repository and Apache 2.0 license.

Found a bug or have an idea? Please report an issue or contribute to the project on GitHub.

One or both experimental desktop settings are not explicitly enabled. Your device may still support external screens, but desktop windowing may not work. You can enable them in Developer options, if available, or using ADB:

adb shell settings put global force_desktop_mode_on_external_displays 1
adb shell settings put global enable_freeform_support 1

Restart your phone after changing them. You can continue without changing these settings.

Mirra will stop the current cast and open Android settings. Removing all saved Wi-Fi Direct groups there may help fix connection problems. You can also rename your device in Wi-Fi Direct settings, if your phone supports it. Mirra will not delete saved groups or ordinary Wi-Fi networks automatically.
In Wi-Fi settings, open Wi-Fi Direct to manage saved groups or rename your device.

Shared lets the phone and display negotiate which device hosts the Wi-Fi Direct group. Try forced host if a receiver, such as a Windows PC, has trouble connecting. Forced host asks the phone to be the group owner; some receivers may not support it.\n\nLong-press this device later to clear a remembered choice.
